configs.description: The PDU as it ships. The 3 m cord beyond its gland is not drawn.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the technical specification (rev 2020-07-01) gives the input as a NEMA L5-20P plug on a 3 m cord entering at the bottom front, and the maker's mechanical drawing MPX2-2475C (Rev A, 2011) titles the input "IEC320 C20", draws a C20 inlet in the strip's bottom end (view A) and a cord with C19 and C20 ends beside it. The device follows the specification, the later document, which the PXE series data sheet (2016) supports for the same 24-outlet Zero U strip (PXE-1475V, NEMA L5-20P). The drawn inlet is not drawn here.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which input this part number ships with.

gaps.note: the drawing shows a small circle beside every outlet, and the quick setup guide says the outlets of a PX2 or PX3 have LEDs. The rings are drawn; no document gives the colours a lamp shows, so they are not filled and are not a part.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the strip, or the guide's description of the outlet lamps.

gaps.note: the control panel drawing shows one lamp that carries no label, between the two display windows and the five labelled lamps. It is drawn as a lamp and its meaning is not stated; the held PX-Series PDU user guide (4.3.11) does not describe the panel's lamps.
gaps.wanted: a PX2 front-panel description that names the unlabelled lamp, or a photograph of the controller panel.

gaps.note: the PX-Series PDU User Guide (4.3.11) says in its comparison of the PX2, PX3 and PXC / PXO that the PX2's SENSOR port is an RJ-12 and the PX3's an RJ-45, and the drawing shows the PX2's sensor jack narrower than its feature jack. It is drawn as the RJ45 serial jack part because no jack part of the library is sized as an RJ-12 housing (`std/rj11@1` is the opening alone), so it is drawn wider than the maker's jack. The feature jack is an RJ-45 by the same guide.
gaps.wanted: a six-position jack part sized as an RJ-12 housing.

gaps.note: the drawing places the two buttons and does not dimension their heads. They are drawn as the maker's PX3 mounting button, 14.7 mm across. Page 7 dimensions a part 250-80-0011-00 with a 14.00 head and a 25.20 flange. It does not say that part is the button. The PX3 part is shared with other devices, so it is not changed here.
gaps.wanted: the kit's installation sheet, which says which of the four parts is the button.

gaps.note: the side view (page 6) prints a depth dimension of 65.3 mm whose extension lines end on the outermost body line. The outlet bodies stand 3.5 mm proud of that line, and the panel steps and lamp rings stand on it. The two mounting buttons stand behind the rear plane. The specification prints a depth of 65 mm, and the device keeps it. A side face is 65 mm deep and clips its decor there, so these parts are cut and not drawn. The kit has no shape for a part beyond a side view's depth. The schema's `overhang` is "HOW FAR REAL PARTS REACH BEYOND THE RACK FACE", only on a `rack` device (`spec/schemas/device.schema.json`, lines 555 to 563). Lint L150 leaves decor out, since decor "is clipped and never drawn" outside the face.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of the depth with the outlet bodies included.

gaps.note: no held picture shows either end of the strip: the drawing has no end view and the specification publishes no feature on an end.
gaps.wanted: an end view of the strip.

capability.note: datasheet - remote outlet switching yes, metering per input line only. So `outlet-switching: true` and each outlet states on and off, and `metering-scope: input`.

chassis.note: drawing - 1539 x 52 x 65 mm (60.6 x 2.1 x 2.6 in), the specification's height, width and depth (page 2); the drawing prints 1539.0, 52.2 and 65.3. 4.2 kg, shipping 7.1 kg and 185 x 120 x 1650 mm. `ru: 35` is the height it runs, 1539 mm being 34.6 units; it is derived, not printed.

colours.note: THE HEX VALUES ARE ESTIMATES OF THE PRINTED COLOUR. The specification gives "Black powder coat (custom colors available)" and no photograph of this model is held, so the chassis is black and the panel, plates and lamps are estimates of dark grey and white; the two display windows are drawn very dark red because the drawing paints them red and no document says what a lit or unlit window looks like. The drawn faces have not been compared with a photograph.

controller.note: drawing - the panel is 188 x 43 mm (page 4) and starts about 396.5 mm from the top end, read from the elevation, to about 1 mm. Its contents are read from the page 4 drawing. They are a reset ring and a window (LINE / CB / UB) with two round buttons under it (UP, BOTH, DOWN). They are a second window and five lamps. The lamps are labelled SENSOR, UB LOAD (%), POWER (kW), VOLTAGE (V) and CURRENT (A), with one unlabelled lamp beside them. They are a FEATURE jack over an ETHERNET jack, a USB-B jack, a SENSOR jack, a USB-A jack and a CONSOLE / MODEM D-sub jack. Each jack is turned the way the drawing turns it. The ports' types are read as follows. The D-sub is a DB9, `std/db9@1`. The PX-Series PDU User Guide's comparison of the PX2, PX3 and PXC / PXO gives the PX2 a male DB9 RS-232 CONSOLE / MODEM port. It gives it one USB-A port at 12 Mbps, one LAN port at 100 Mbps and an RJ-12 SENSOR port. So the USB-A is the USB 2 skin of `std/usb-a@1`. The FEATURE jack is an RJ-45 by the guide's note. It is drawn, with the SENSOR jack, as an RJ45 serial jack like the maker's other PDUs (gaps: sensor-jack-type). The USB-B is the maker's USB-B part. The panel's corners are rounded 2.2 mm and each window's 1.5 mm (page 4 raster, 11.8 px per mm). Each window carries seven-segment digit outlines as the page 6 elevation draws them. The LINE / CB / UB window has two rows of two digits. The other has three rows of two. That makes ten digits in all. Each digit is 5.5 mm wide and 8.3 mm high. The rows are 10.6 mm apart. Each row has one point at its upper right. Their top and bottom edges slope as the drawing draws them, 8.4 degrees at a row's left digit and 10.6 at its right one. The angles are estimated from page 6 at 14400 dpi. The sides lean less than 1.5 degrees, so they are drawn upright. The red outlines are read from page 6 at 4800 dpi, 12.36 px per mm. They form two groups, 11.25 by 19.34 mm and 11.17 by 30.19 mm, each two digits wide. A digit's box is read from its group, an estimate good to about 0.2 mm. The specification's text says "3-digit LED user-selectable display" (page 1). Its drawing shows five rows of two cells. A hairline edge 0.3 mm outside each window is drawn as the page 4 picture draws it. The console jack's flange is 31.5 by 6.6 mm with two holes 25.0 apart. It is drawn behind its shell. The picture is scaled from the printed 188 mm panel width. A T-shaped line between the two round buttons (a bar 2.8 mm across, a stem 6.3 mm long, from page 6) is drawn. A ring 4.2 mm across round each screw hole is drawn from page 4, which draws the holes. Page 6 does not. One outline, 34.4 by 16.9 mm from page 6, holds the FEATURE and ETHERNET jacks. The reset button is a ring 2.4 mm across, as the drawing shows it, with no pinhole. These four are estimates read from the drawings. The two jacks' own plates lie inside the shared outline. The Raritan logo, the label texts, the two arrowheads and the UP, BOTH, DOWN and RESET labels are not drawn. This change draws shapes only. A later change draws marks, colours and the rest.

front.note: drawing - outlet centres at 100.6 + 35.0 n mm for outlets 1 to 8, 677.4 + 35.0 n for 9 to 16 and 1067.1 + 35.0 n for 17 to 24 (n from 0), read from the small marks on the strip's edge that sit over each outlet's centre; the drawing prints the pitch 35.00 and the span 245.00 of a group of eight (PDF page 6, view B). Outlet 1's mark is not legible and is the second's less 35.0. Positions ACROSS the strip are not printed: each outlet is centred, as the drawing's outlet frames are. The numeral of each outlet stands 17 mm toward the top of the strip from its centre, as the drawing prints it.

input.note: datasheet - NEMA L5-20P (2P3W), 3 m (9.84 ft), bottom-front feed, cord retention yes, IP44 cable, maximum input 20 A, 100 - 120 V. The maker's drawing titles the input IEC320 C20 instead (gaps: input-conflict).

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S PRINTED SIZES AND A READING OF ITS MECHANICAL DRAWING. The technical specification (rev 2020-07-01) prints the unit size; its mechanical diagram MPX2-2475C (Rev A, 2 June 2011; PDF page 6) prints the length, the outlet group span and pitch and the mounting buttons, and draws the strip's elevation, from which each position along it is read at 3.09 px per mm to about 1 mm. Its control panel (PDF page 4, 188 x 43 mm) is read at 11.8 px per mm. The library draws the PDU STANDING, cord end down, so a position along the strip is the y of the front view: the drawing is turned a quarter turn, outlet 1 at the top. No vendor stencil was opened and no vendor drawing, photograph or stencil is copied; the figures were read by a person and written down. No photograph of this model is held.

mount.note: datasheet - `rack-side`: a zero-U strip with two mounting buttons on its back (kit G2-RACK-FOR-ZU, page 2; page 7 lists the parts 250-70-0104-00, 250-80-0011-00, 250-70-0007-00 and 250-70-0093-00 without saying which is which).

outlets.note: datasheet - the technical specification: (24) NEMA 5-20R, 16 A, remote switching, no metering per outlet and no branch breaker ("Overload Protection N/A", "Metering per Output Receptacle No"). Drawn as std/nema-5-20r@1 in its own orientation: the drawing shows the earth hole at the end toward outlet 1, the T slot toward the face's edge that is the strip's right, and the line slot to its left, which is that part unturned when the strip stands.

rear.note: drawing - two mounting buttons 1244.0 apart, the first 145.0 from the top end (PDF page 6, rear view, read at 2400 dpi). The side view puts the stubs at 147 and 1391 mm. The device stood them at 45.0 and 1289.0, a misreading of the pale printed 1. The button is the maker's PX3 mounting button, its 14.7 head borrowed (gaps: mounting-button-size). It is centred across, an estimate. The rear view draws concentric rings and a cross-head screw on each button; the shared part draws a plain disc. A ring 25.2 mm across is drawn round each, the 25.20 that page 7 prints for the button's flange. Hairlines at 1.0, 1.6 and 5.5 mm from each long edge are drawn as the rear view draws them, read at 3.09 px per mm.

sides.note: estimated - the left face is the side elevation of page 6, the view below the front elevation, so the strip's left in third angle. It is read at 3.0897 px per mm from the printed 1539.0 mm. Its lines and its depth dimension are read at 4800 dpi, 12.36 px per mm. It shows six lines along the profile, at 2.0, 6.5, 8.7, 59.95, 61.5 and 63.5 mm from the rear. It shows a fixing block of 2.6 by 4.5 mm at each outlet's centre. It shows a cap at the bottom end and an end plate at each end. It shows 12 round marks with a triangle. The front plane is the outermost body line, 65.3 mm from the rear. The printed 65.3 depth dimension's two extension lines end on that line and on the rear line. The 24 outlet bodies stand 3.5 mm proud of that plane. The panel steps and the lamp rings beside the outlets stand on it too. All of them lie beyond the 65 mm depth and are not drawn (gaps: side-reach). The right face turns the same parts round, except the 12 marks. No held picture shows the marks on that side. The front elevation shows the fixing blocks end-on, 2.6 mm long at each outlet's centre on both long edges. It shows an end plate at each end. The rear view shows the end plates.
